features.text: Patient has asthma with symptoms including phlegm buildup, coughing, chest tightness, wheezing, and lightheadedness during physical activity.
Patient uses an albuterol inhaler, typically two puffs during an attack.
Patient experiences symptoms primarily during aerobic exercise and exposure to smoke.
Patient reports that the albuterol inhaler helps with symptoms but causes shakiness as a side effect.
Patient has seasonal allergies and some fluid in the ears.
Patient has been feeling sad, unmotivated, and tired, with difficulty engaging in social activities.
Patient is experiencing stress related to academic pressures, including SATs and AP classes.
Patient has no history of daily asthma medications such as Singulair.
Patient has no history of tonsils.
Patient's heart, lungs, ears, eyes, and abdomen were found to be normal during the physical exam.
Patient prefers to avoid people who smoke and steps away from such environments.
Patient is interested in exploring options for managing asthma and mood issues.
Patient is currently participating in water polo but has had to stop during matches due to asthma symptoms.
Patient is a student with academic pressures and is enrolled in AP classes.
Patient is open to starting therapy and completing screening questionnaires for mood issues.
